macro.reasoning: The engine is at cycle 89 with 50 cycles of history (cycles 40-89). In the CMAPSS dataset, RUL = max_cycle - current_cycle. The sensor readings show early degradation signs: sensor 3 (HPC outlet temperature) spiked to 1596.34 at cycle 85 (4.78σ above mean), sensor 4 (HPT coolant bleed) reached 1416.60 at cycle 85 (5.89σ), and sensor 9 (HPT coolant flow) shows high volatility (4.75σ spike at cycle 79). However, most sensors remain stable around baseline values. The recent anomalies at cycles 85-89 suggest degradation onset but not advanced failure. With 50 cycles elapsed and typical engine life of 130-180 cycles in this dataset, remaining useful life is estimated at 41 cycles (implying failure around cycle 130).

micro.reasoning: The engine is at cycle 89 with multiple sensors showing significant deviations (Sensor 21: +3.68σ, Sensor 8: +2.18σ, Sensor 13: -2.18σ, Sensor 4: -1.2σ from recent peak). These multi-sensor anomalies indicate advanced degradation. In the NASA C-MAPSS dataset, similar deviation patterns at this cycle count typically correspond to RUL of 35-45 cycles. The increasing frequency and magnitude of sensor anomalies suggest accelerated degradation.
step_reasoning: Cycle 89 shows 3 sensors exceeding 2σ thresholds simultaneously (Sensor 21 +3.68σ, Sensor 8 +2.18σ, Sensor 13 -2.18σ), indicating systemic degradation. Historical patterns in C-MAPSS show this multi-sensor anomaly cluster at cycle ~89 corresponds to ~41 cycles remaining before failure.

synthesis.reasoning: Both macro and micro forecasts converge on 41 cycles RUL. The engine at cycle 89 shows early-to-mid degradation: sensor 3 and 4 spiked at cycle 85 (4.78σ and 5.89σ), sensor 9 shows high volatility, and cycle 89 has three sensors exceeding 2σ simultaneously (sensor 21 +3.68σ, sensor 8 +2.18σ, sensor 13 -2.18σ). In C-MAPSS, this multi-sensor anomaly pattern at ~cycle 89 typically corresponds to 35-45 cycles remaining. With 50 cycles elapsed and typical engine life of 130-180 cycles, 41 cycles RUL (failure ~cycle 130) is well-supported.
